Made for a Real-Life James Bond: Skyfall Mansion Is a Fanboy's Wildest $3 Million Dream
25 photos
Photo: Fine&Country
As James Bond is getting ready to enter into a new, Amazon-owned era with actor Robert Pattinson, now's as good a time as ever to check out what must be the wildest, most insane James Bond tribute-mansion ever. It's called Skyfall and it's back on the market for the second time in as many years.
Skyfall, the mansion, is often described in the British media as an architectural masterpiece, a theatrical piece of real estate that blends the luxuries of modern life with the most exquisite materials and artwork, James Bond movie references and actual film memorabilia collected over the years. It is theatrical alright, and will do a similarly passionate 007 fan – and multi-millionaire – proud.
As luck would have it, Skyfall is for sale again, one year after being listed publicly and with a considerable price cut. Times are rough for multi-millionaires as well, and the owner of this mansion, a self-professed James Bond fan that's often referenced in the media as a "Daniel Craig lookalike," is even willing to part with the mansion with many of the items shown in photos and the video below.
That doesn't include his personal car collection , three cars from which are shown in the tour in the detached, climate-controlled three-car garage on the property. Dean Reep, the owner of the mansion, has spent about as much money and time to put together an auto gallery worthy of a real-life James Bond.
Photo: Fine&Country It includes, besides Ferraris, Land Rovers, and one ghost-white Countach, a 007 Land Rover with the N007 license plate and one Aston Martin DBS with another 007-inspired plate.
The mansion, located in Nottinghamshire some distance from London, sits on a property Reep bought in 2017 and then proceeded to turn into his dream family home, which also happens to be the wildest James Bond tribute . It was first listed one year ago and is back on the market now, but it is still not complete. It can also be further modified to increase the number of bedrooms.
As it is now, Skyfall features two formal reception rooms, a chef's kitchen with premium appliances and custom cabinetry, a games room, a separate gym with a detached bedroom, six bedrooms with ensuite bathrooms, two separate greenhouses, and a bar with another games room with a wraparound gallery that doubles as a James Bond museum.
Photo: Fine&Country The listing mentions that the gallery can be turned into three more bedrooms, should the next owner wish to have a higher occupancy.
Another highlight is the garage and the spacious motorcourt, with the former offering extra space on top that can be turned into a staff annex or separate accommodation for extended family . A large outdoor lounge space, a pavilion, and a Wimbledon-like tennis court are also available, with perfectly manicured gardens offering privacy and gorgeous spaces for walking.
The listing also describes Skyfall as "grandiose," which is definitely accurate. The styling is not subtle, despite what the same listing will have you believe, as neither are the film references.
Photo: Fine&Country But there is beauty behind this agglomeration of artifacts and memorabilia, from the gorgeous carved staircase to the stained glass windows, the silk tapestry on the walls, or the elaborate carvings integrated even in the most surprising spaces, like the ground-floor bathroom.
Speaking of that bathroom, it also comes with a secret door that leads down to a 3,000 square-foot (279 square-meter) cellar.
The master suite offers, in addition to a massive walk-in his and hers wardrobe two people could easily call home and an ensuite spa bathroom, an actual leather chair used during production of the film Spectre and stunt jackets from Quantum of Solace and Skyfall .
Photo: Fine&Country Normally, collectibles as valuables as these would not be included with the sale of the house they're in, but the owner says he's willing to part with them. Also part of the sale are Sir Roger Moore's gold-plated Seiko Moonraker watch, Rare Aston Martin DB5 blueprints, original Aston Martin Lagonda factory memorabilia, more film set items from Skyfall and Quantum of Solace , and signed memorabilia from Bond actors.
Up in the gallery that overlooks the antique snooker table in the bar is a home office where the owner installed an Aston Martin seat from one of the vehicles Jeremy Clarkson used on Top Gear. From what you can see in the video tour, the owner and his wife are not just James Bond fans, but passionate cinephiles and passionate collectors of car-related memorabilia, so this pick should not come as a surprise.
Highlights of the mansion include a pair of stag statues that overlook the electric gates and are a tribute to the home in the film Skyfall , giant portraits from the James Bond universe on the walls, rare fabrics and materials used in the most creative ways, beautiful artwork, and 11,000 square feet (1,022 square meters) in total of living space, spread between the main house and the annex.
Photo: Fine&Country When Skyfall was first listed, it was asking £3 million (€3.6 million or $4 million at the current exchange rate). That asking price has now been reduced to £2.25 million (€2.7 million or $3 million).
